edits.finding: decision 6 (eta convention) (Eq. (138) rewritten in place)
edits.old:
$$n_{\rm coh}=\frac{\eta\rho E_{\rm pt}}{E_{\rm ph}}\frac{A_{\rm mode}}{\pi R^2},\qquad A_{\rm mode}\sim\frac{\lambda^2}{\Omega_{\rm cell}} \tag{138}$$

  If the received mode is widened to fill every angular cell, its best-order scaling is $A_{\rm mode}\sim\lambda^2/\Omega_{\rm cell}$, and the two cell-angle factors (in $E_{\rm pt}$ and in $A_{\rm mode}$) cancel. That is the ideal full-coverage scaling used below, subject to polarization, beam shape, truncation and receive-mode overlap.

$$n_{\rm coh}=\frac{\eta\rho E_{\rm pt}}{E_{\rm ph}}\frac{A_{\rm mode}}{\pi R^2},\qquad A_{\rm mode}\simeq\frac{t^2}{2}\,\frac{\lambda^2}{\Omega_{\rm cell}} \tag{138}$$

  If the received mode is widened until its Gaussian 1/e² spot fills one angular cell, the Gaussian model of §C10.3b gives the second relation (its Eq. (147) with a footprint fraction of one), where $t^2/2=0.419$ is the round-trip truncation $t^2=0.838$ times the single-polarization factor ½; at 0.05° it is 1.32 mm². The two cell-angle factors (in $E_{\rm pt}$ and in $A_{\rm mode}$) then cancel. That is the ideal full-coverage scaling used below, subject to beam shape and receive-mode overlap at the cell corners.

edits.finding: decision 6 (eta convention); decision 7 (ToF at 940 nm, n_req 21.7, eta 0.164)
edits.old:
- Common inputs: $\Omega_{\rm FOV}=(120^\circ\times25^\circ)(\pi/180)^2=0.914$ sr (small-angle approximation: the product of the two field angles in radians), $R=200$ m, $f_{\rm frame}=10$ Hz and $\rho=0.1$, so $\pi R^2f_{\rm frame}\,\Omega_{\rm FOV}/\rho=1.15\times10^{7}\ {\rm m^2\,s^{-1}\,sr}$.
- Coherent: $E_{\rm ph}=hc/\lambda=1.28\times10^{-19}$ J and $\lambda^2=2.40\times10^{-12}$ m² at 1550 nm. With $N_{\rm req}=10$ and $\eta=0.3$, $P_{\rm coh}=10\times1.28\times10^{-19}\times1.15\times10^{7}/(2.40\times10^{-12}\times0.3)=20.4$ W; with $N_{\rm req}=30$ and $\eta=0.1$ it is nine times larger, 184 W.
- ToF: $E_{\rm ph}=2.19\times10^{-19}$ J at 905 nm and $A_{\rm rx}=\pi(12.5\ {\rm mm})^2=4.91\times10^{-4}$ m² for the 25 mm aperture. At 0.1° × 0.1°, $\Omega_{\rm cell}=(1.745\times10^{-3})^2=3.05\times10^{-6}$ sr, so $P_{\rm ToF}=20\times2.19\times10^{-19}\times1.15\times10^{7}/(4.91\times10^{-4}\times3.05\times10^{-6}\times0.15)=0.225$ W. Halving one cell side doubles $P_{\rm ToF}$, and halving both quadruples it.
- Ratio: $P_{\rm coh}/P_{\rm ToF}$ falls in proportion to $\Omega_{\rm cell}$. At 0.05° × 0.05°, $20.4/0.90=23$ and $184/0.90=204\approx200$.
edits.new:
- Common inputs: $\Omega_{\rm FOV}=(120^\circ\times25^\circ)(\pi/180)^2=0.914$ sr (small-angle approximation: the product of the two field angles in radians), $R=200$ m, $f_{\rm frame}=10$ Hz and $\rho=0.1$, so $\pi R^2f_{\rm frame}\,\Omega_{\rm FOV}/\rho=1.148\times10^{7}\ {\rm m^2\,s^{-1}\,sr}$.
- Coherent: $E_{\rm ph}=hc/\lambda=1.282\times10^{-19}$ J and $\lambda^2=2.403\times10^{-12}$ m² at 1550 nm, and $t^2/2=0.419$. With $N_{\rm req}=10$ and $\eta=0.25$, $P_{\rm coh}=10\times1.282\times10^{-19}\times1.148\times10^{7}/(0.419\times2.403\times10^{-12}\times0.25)=58.5$ W, i.e. 5.85 W per detected photon per sample; $N_{\rm req}=30$ triples it, to 175.5 W. With the measured efficiency 0.112 instead of 0.25, both rise $0.25/0.112=2.23$-fold, to 131 and 392 W.
- ToF: $E_{\rm ph}=2.113\times10^{-19}$ J at 940 nm and $A_{\rm rx}=\pi(12.5\ {\rm mm})^2=4.909\times10^{-4}$ m² for the 25 mm aperture. At 0.1° × 0.1°, $\Omega_{\rm cell}=(1.745\times10^{-3})^2=3.046\times10^{-6}$ sr, so $P_{\rm ToF}=21.7\times2.113\times10^{-19}\times1.148\times10^{7}/(4.909\times10^{-4}\times3.046\times10^{-6}\times0.164)=0.215$ W. Halving one cell side doubles $P_{\rm ToF}$, and halving both quadruples it.
- Ratio: $P_{\rm coh}/P_{\rm ToF}$ falls in proportion to $\Omega_{\rm cell}$. At 0.1° × 0.1°, $58.5/0.215=272$ and $175.5/0.215=816$; at 0.05° × 0.05°, $58.5/0.860=68$ and $175.5/0.860=204$.
edits.why: Substitutions for the recomputed table.

edits.old: Power parity arrives only near **0.004–0.01°**, where a 25 mm ToF receiver itself approaches the diffraction limit ($A_{\rm rx}\Omega_{\rm cell}\to\lambda^2$): its étendue per cell then shrinks to a single mode, the same as a coherent receiver's. Because the ratio scales as $\theta_{\rm cell}^2$, with $\theta_{\rm cell}$ the cell width, parity needs $\theta_{\rm cell}=0.1^\circ/\sqrt{87}=0.011^\circ$ to $0.1^\circ/\sqrt{800}=0.0035^\circ$; the diffraction limit itself is at $\theta_{\rm cell}=\lambda/\sqrt{A_{\rm rx}}=0.905\ \mu{\rm m}/22\ {\rm mm}=4.1\times10^{-5}$ rad $=0.0023^\circ$. That is beyond even "camera-like" resolution.
edits.new: Power parity arrives only near **0.0035–0.006°**, where a 25 mm ToF receiver itself approaches the diffraction limit ($A_{\rm rx}\Omega_{\rm cell}\to\lambda^2$): its étendue per cell then shrinks to a single mode, the same as a coherent receiver's. Because the ratio scales as $\theta_{\rm cell}^2$, with $\theta_{\rm cell}$ the cell width, parity needs $\theta_{\rm cell}=0.1^\circ/\sqrt{272}=0.0061^\circ$ to $0.1^\circ/\sqrt{816}=0.0035^\circ$; the diffraction limit itself is at $\theta_{\rm cell}=\lambda/\sqrt{A_{\rm rx}}=0.940\ \mu{\rm m}/22.2\ {\rm mm}=4.2\times10^{-5}$ rad $=0.0024^\circ$. That is beyond even "camera-like" resolution, and finer than the 0.0125° of "2,000+ line" claims, at which full-coverage coherent detection still needs 4.2–13× ToF's power.

- A 20 mm monostatic aperture at 100–200 m sees about 3–6 speckles and keeps about 1/5 to 1/11 of the hard-aperture power; only in the far field does the loss approach the ≈3× of polarization and mode shape.
- A mirror-scanned coherent system's efficiency-weighted aperture is therefore about **15–40 mm² at 100–300 m**, not the ≈80 mm² of the far-field formula alone (both are worked in §C10.3a, item 7). A 25 mm ToF unit's ≈85 mm² is about 2–6× larger ($86/41=2.1$ to $86/14.5=5.9$) before sunlight is considered; sunlight favours coherent detection.
- With truncation and single polarization included, the *area-matched* coherent mode-equivalent collecting area at 0.05° is 1.3 mm². It is 1.6 mm² without the truncation factor $t^2=0.84$, and 3.2 mm² without the single-polarization factor ½ as well; that last value is the ideal $\lambda^2/\Omega_{\rm cell}$ of §C10.2, item 5, where $\Omega_{\rm cell}=\theta_{\rm cell}^2$ is the solid angle of one mesh cell.
edits.new:
- A mirror-scanned coherent receiver's efficiency-weighted aperture is about **7–21 mm² at 100–300 m** (Result 2's $A_{\rm mode}$ times $\eta=0.25$), not the ≈27 mm² of the far-field formula alone (both are worked in §C10.3a, item 7). A 25 mm ToF unit's ≈80 mm² is about 4–11× larger ($80/20.5=3.9$ to $80/7.2=11$), and the four receivers per point of §C7a narrow this to 1.3× at 200 m. ToF's $\eta=0.164$ already contains the bright-sun live fraction (≈71 mm² in a fully sunlit scene); sunlight's other cost, a higher detection threshold, sits in the photon requirement (§C10.3a, item 7, caveats).
- With truncation and single polarization included, the *area-matched* coherent mode-equivalent collecting area at 0.05° is 1.3 mm². It is 1.6 mm² without the truncation factor $t^2=0.84$, and 3.2 mm² without the single-polarization factor ½ as well; that last value is the ideal $\lambda^2/\Omega_{\rm cell}$, where $\Omega_{\rm cell}=\theta_{\rm cell}^2$ is the solid angle of one mesh cell. The cell-filling estimates of §C10.2, item 5 and §C10.3 use the 1.3 mm².
